description:

Perle is an AI infrastructure company building expert-driven training data, evaluation systems, and applied AI products for the world's leading labs and enterprises. Headquartered in San Francisco with experts across more than forty markets, we specialize in the work that requires real human judgment: domain expertise, linguistic nuance, and cultural fidelity that generic data vendors cannot deliver.
Apply here:
THE ROLE
We are hiring expert Bosnian transcribers to convert audio recordings of native speakers into precise, conventionally formatted written transcripts. The work powers speech recognition, dialogue, and evaluation systems for major AI labs. Audio ranges from clean studio recordings to natural conversational speech in real-world acoustic conditions.
You will be working at the level of expert linguistic judgment. This is not data entry. Decisions about orthography, code-switching, speaker attribution, disfluencies, and non-speech events shape the quality of every model trained on your output.
DIALECT AND SCOPE
Bosnian as spoken across Bosnia and Herzegovina, with characteristic features including Turkish loanwords. Project audio reflects regional varieties and conversational speech, written primarily in Latin script with Cyrillic also in use.
Primary speaker regions: Sarajevo, Banja Luka, Tuzla, Zenica, Mostar, Bihac.
WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Transcribe audio recordings into accurate, time-aligned written text following Perle's project-specific style guide

• Apply correct conventions for speaker identification, overlapping speech, disfluencies, fillers, false starts, and non-speech events such as laughter, background noise, and music

• Make principled orthographic decisions for dialectal, colloquial, and code-switched speech

• Flag ambiguous segments, uncertain speakers, and audio quality issues using project conventions

• Self-review every submission against Perle's quality bar before delivery

• Engage with QA reviewers on edge cases, calibration sessions, and style guide updates

MUST HAVE

• Native fluency in Bosnian with lifelong residence or deep immersion in Bosnia and Herzegovina

• Mastery of Bosnian Latin orthography and awareness of Cyrillic where applicable

• Ability to distinguish Bosnian from Croatian and Serbian in mixed audio

• Familiarity with Turkish and Arabic loanwords as they appear in everyday Bosnian speech

• At least two years of professional transcription, captioning, court reporting, broadcast, translation, or linguistic annotation experience

• Demonstrated accuracy at the word level under deadline pressure

• Comfortable with web-based annotation platforms and variable-speed audio playback

• Reliable high-speed internet, quality headphones, and a quiet workspace

• Ability to commit to defined volume per week during active project phases

NICE TO HAVE

• Background in South Slavic linguistics, translation, journalism, or media

• Prior experience annotating BCS speech data

• Working knowledge of Croatian, Serbian, or Turkish for cross-lingual audio

• Familiarity with IPA or other phonetic transcription systems

• Experience with verbatim versus clean-verbatim transcription conventions

HOW WE WORK WITH YOU

• Paid pilot task before full onboarding so both sides can calibrate

• Per-task or per-minute compensation, with rates tied to audio complexity and turnaround

• Flexible scheduling, with volume scaling up and down based on active client projects

• Direct working relationship with Perle's linguistic leads and QA team

• Eligible for invitation to additional Perle expert projects across related domains

Note: This application is for Rural Partners Corps (RPC) host sites for the 2026-27 Program Year, featuring a December 2026 - August 2027 term of service. We welcome applications from partners nationwide. Submitting this form is a way to indicate general interest only -organizations are not committing to participate by applying. We encourage interested partners to complete this form as soon as possible.
About the Rural Partners Corps
Rural Partners Corps (RPC) is a new AmeriCorps service fellowship from Lead For America (LFA) that places locally rooted Members with rural, place-based backbone organizations.
Members already live in or near the communities they serve. They bring local knowledge, transferable skills, relationships, and a commitment to making their communities stronger.
RPC Members serve 40 hours per week from December through August, working alongside Host Site staff and community partners to build organizational and community capacity and advance cradle-to-career economic mobility for rural young people.
Who Should Apply?
RPC Host Sites are place-based backbone organizations serving rural communities or regions. Eligible entities include:

• Regional or community-based nonprofits

• Community Development Corporations (CDCs) & Economic Development Organizations (EDOs)

• Cradle-to-career partnerships & collective impact initiatives

• Community foundations & philanthropic organizations

• Tribal governments & Native-led organizations

• Local government agencies & regional councils of government

• Education organizations (K12 through Higher Education Institutions)

What Does Your Organization Gain?
Dedicated Capacity: A full-time Member focused on meaningful projects that advance your organization's priorities.
Stronger Partnerships: Additional capacity to build relationships, convene partners, and connect community assets.
Organizational Infrastructure: Tools, systems, research, processes, volunteer infrastructure, and other resources that strengthen your organization's capacity.
Local Talent: A motivated community member who already knows and cares about the place-and wants to contribute to its future.
LFA Support: Your Member receives ongoing coaching and professional development through LFA, while your organization has a dedicated LFA Program Coordinator as an additional source of support.
What Will an RPC Member Do?
An RPC Member joins your organization as a locally rooted capacity-building partner.
They are not an intern, temporary worker, outside consultant, or replacement for existing staff. Instead, they bring their skills, relationships, local knowledge, and initiative to help your organization move important community priorities forward.
Members will typically:
1. Know the Place

• Conduct community asset mapping and listening

• Learn the community's strengths, priorities, relationships, and existing initiatives

2. Build Relationships

• Engage community stakeholders and partners

• Support cross-sector collaboration and community convenings

• Connect people, organizations, and resources

3. Understand & Advance Priorities

• Support strategic planning and implementation

• Coordinate projects and initiatives

• Conduct research and organize information

• Help move locally defined priorities from ideas to action

4. Build Capacity

• Develop tools, processes, resources, and systems

• Strengthen partnership, communication, or volunteer infrastructure and engagement

• Support training, workshops, outreach, and community engagement

5. Support Cradle-to-Career & Economic Mobility

• Contribute to initiatives involving youth, education, workforce development, career pathways, and economic mobility

• Help strengthen connections across schools, nonprofits, employers, government, higher education, and other community partners

The Member's approach is: Know the Place → Build Relationships → Understand Priorities → Organize → Connect → Execute → Build Capacity
Specific assignments will be shaped by you
